title: Why AI eats middle management and how to run a startup without managers
summary: Paul Buchheit explains why the information-gathering and coordination work of middle managers is what LLMs do well, drawing on Google's early flat-org experiments. He argues startups should go AI-native, using AI as a cognitive multiplier to monitor work, and focus on the people who create value.

principles.text: Middle management's core job, gathering and combining information, is what AI does best, so coordinators are more replaceable than the people doing the work.
principles.quote: a lot of the roles of middle management, which is basically just like gathering information from people and then combining it and then passing along to the person above can be done by AI as well.

principles.text: Hire great engineers so you need less coordination; flat orgs can work at surprising scale, though someone still must handle performance and HR.
principles.quote: one of the beliefs early on at Google was if we just had really great engineers, you would need less of that. And I And I think that's still true.

principles.text: Removing layers of middle management lets companies grow larger without the complexity, slowness and politics those layers add.
principles.quote: historically one of the reasons that big companies get uh complex and inefficient and political is that you have these layers and layers of of middle management

principles.text: Run an AI-native startup: keep scaling and solve each problem as it appears with AI instead of adding management layers.
principles.quote: as a startup, you just keep scaling and fixing the problems as they occur with with AI. I mean, that's I think what we would call the AI native approach, solve all of your problems with AI.

principles.text: Use AI as a cognitive multiplier: imagine how you'd do the job with unlimited time, then give those same instructions to the AI.
principles.quote: the way I like to think about using AI is is kind of just as a cognitive multiplier. So, if you think to yourself, "Well, how would I do the job if I just had unlimited time?"

principles.text: Figure out who creates the value and focus your attention and resources there; fewer layers means everything moves faster.
principles.quote: you have to figure out who who's creating the value and then hopefully that's the part of the organization where you're able to really focus uh you know, your attention and your resources.
